title: JavaScript Array & Data Handling: Quick Revision
summary: Night-before revision of JavaScript's array transforms (map/filter/reduce, find, some/every, sort), spread and destructuring, shallow vs deep copy with structuredClone, Object.entries, and Map/Set vs plain objects.

chapters.title: Array Methods Mental Model
points: map(fn) returns a new array of the same length, one transformed value per element: [1,2,3].map(x => x*2) → [2,4,6]
filter(fn) returns a new array with only elements where fn is truthy; length can shrink to 0
reduce((acc, x) => ..., init) folds an array into one value; acc carries the result between calls
Always pass an initial value to reduce: on an empty array with no init it throws TypeError
map, filter and reduce do not mutate the original array; forEach returns undefined so it cannot be chained

chapters.title: Searching, Testing and Sorting
points: find(fn) returns the first matching element or undefined; findIndex(fn) returns its index or -1
some(fn) returns true if at least one element passes; every(fn) returns true only if all pass; both short-circuit
every on an empty array returns true and some on an empty array returns false
sort() with no comparator sorts as strings: [10,9,1].sort() → [1,10,9]; use sort((a,b) => a-b) for ascending numbers
sort mutates the array in place and returns the same reference; copy first with [...arr].sort(...) or arr.toSorted(...)

chapters.title: Spread and Destructuring
points: Array spread copies or merges: [...a, ...b]; object spread merges with later keys winning: {...defaults, ...overrides}
Array destructuring is positional: const [first, , third] = arr; skip slots with an empty comma
Object destructuring is by key with rename and default: const { name: n, age = 18 } = user
Rest collects the remainder: const [head, ...tail] = arr and const { id, ...others } = obj; rest must be last
Defaults apply only to undefined, not null: const { x = 5 } = { x: null } gives x = null

chapters.title: Shallow vs Deep Copy and structuredClone
points: Assignment b = a copies the reference, not the data; mutating b also mutates a
Spread, Object.assign, slice and Array.from make shallow copies: top level is new, nested objects are still shared
Shallow copy trap: const c = {...o}; c.inner.x = 1 also changes o.inner.x
structuredClone(value) makes a true deep copy, handling Date, Map, Set, RegExp and circular references
structuredClone throws DataCloneError on functions and drops class prototypes and getters
JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x)) is a lossy deep copy: Date becomes a string, undefined and functions are dropped, Map and Set become {} or [], and circular references throw

chapters.title: Object.entries and Map/Set vs Plain Objects
points: Object.entries(obj) returns [key, value] pairs of own enumerable string keys; Object.keys and Object.values return just keys or values
Round trip: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(obj).map(([k, v]) => [k, v*2])) transforms every value of an object
Map accepts any key type (objects, functions, NaN) and keeps insertion order; plain object keys are coerced to strings or symbols
Map has .size, .get, .set, .has, .delete and is directly iterable; an object needs Object.keys(o).length and inherits prototype keys like toString
Set stores unique values: [...new Set(arr)] dedupes an array, and .has is O(1) versus includes on an array being O(n)
Use a plain object for fixed-shape records and JSON; use Map for dynamic keys, non-string keys or frequent add and delete

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet
points: map → new array, same length; filter → subset; reduce(fn, init) → single value; always give reduce an init
find → element or undefined; findIndex → index or -1; some → any pass; every → all pass (true on empty)
Sort numbers with (a,b) => a-b; sort mutates, so use [...arr].sort() or toSorted()
Spread and Object.assign copy one level; structuredClone copies deep but rejects functions; JSON clone loses Date, undefined, Map, Set
Object.entries / fromEntries to transform objects; Map for any-type keys and frequent changes; Set to dedupe with [...new Set(arr)]
